2011_017_030111regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education Regular Meeting of March 1, 2011, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The consent agenda carries the February 1 and February 15, 2011 minutes, the January 2011 Treasurer's Report with its full Pentamation check register, and two bid awards: copy paper to D & P Management at $50,400.00 and a $162,523.78 Smart interactive white board purchase split between Smart Ed Services ($139,776.78) and City Animation ($22,747.00). The central item is Assistant Superintendent Mark Rajter's Budget Reduction Plan for 2011/2012, which projects a $13.6 million operating deficit and proposes $4,161,953 in adjustments and 40.55 FTE in staff reductions.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, March 1, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. Recognition of Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grant recipients opens the agenda: the Foundation awards $500 grants in every school and funded 77 grants this fall, with President Mike Cianciolo presenting.

**Consent Agenda (Item 5)**
Minutes of the February 1, 2011 regular meeting and the February 15, 2011 workshop; Treasurer's Report for January 2011; award of the copy paper bid; award of the Smart Interactive White Board bid. The February 1 minutes record the appointment of M'Liz Malven to the vacant seat (term ending December 31, 2011) by a 5-1 roll call after a 3-3 defeat of the Kumar Bhatt nomination; a 2010/2011 budget amendment (Resolution 11-022) setting the General Fund at $135,897,825, Special Revenue at $5,530,101, Debt Service at $18,596,717, Capital Projects at $7,216,120 and Internal Service at $120,000; continuation of the Headlee/Adair litigation with Secrest, Wardle, Lynch, Hampton, Truex & Morley for not more than an additional $5,000 (Resolution 11-023); and a $28,300.00 carpet replacement award to Conventional Carpet from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund.

**Bid Awards**
Bid #9702, copy paper (8 1/2 x 11, 20#, 92 brightness, 2,520 cases): bids opened February 17, 2011, sent to 17 potential bidders with 12 responding; award recommended to D & P Management at $50,400.00. Smart interactive white boards: 41 additional systems for buildings using internal account funds or PTO donations, none using bond funds — 23 Qomo document cameras from City Animation on the REMC contract at $22,747.00 and 41 Smart Board systems with installation from Smart Ed Services at $139,776.78.

**Personnel and Curriculum**
Resignation of Frank Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing & Budget (hired December 8, 1999), effective March 14, 2011. District Goals Update presented by assessment coordinator Kris Karbon: all schools made AYP in all sub-groups in 2009-2010, while the goal of scoring in the top 5% on all MDE subtests "was not met in its entirety." Schools of Choice resolution under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, anticipating seats in grades 6–8 at Baker Middle School for 2011-2012.

**Budget Reduction Plan for 2011/2012 (report only, no action)**
Rajter projects a $13.6 million operating deficit for 2011-2012, or $16.0 million using Governor Snyder's proposed $470 per pupil foundation reduction. Proposed adjustments total $4,161,953 ($2,748,140 expenditure reductions, $1,413,813 revenue enhancements) and 40.55 FTE. Informational community meetings follow at 7:00 p.m. on March 7 (Baker), March 8 (Boulan Park), March 9 (Larson) and March 10 (Smith). The meeting closes with a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).
2011_017_030111regmtg.verbose:
Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education Regular Meeting packet for March 1, 2011, called for 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (board offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. The agenda runs: Pledge of Allegiance; recognition of Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grant recipients (p. 3); additions and deletions adding Item 6.A. under Personnel for an administrative resignation (p. 4); consent agenda (p. 5) comprising the February 1, 2011 minutes (p. 6), February 15, 2011 workshop minutes (p. 14), January 2011 Treasurer's Report (p. 15), copy paper bid award (p. 87) and Smart Interactive White Board bid award (p. 89); Personnel (p. 91); Curriculum — District Goals Update (p. 94) and Schools of Choice, Baker Middle School IB–MYP (p. 110); Business — Budget Reduction Plan for 2011/2012 (p. 111); and closed session on negotiations (p. 137).

**Recognition.** The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence awards $500 grants funding curriculum-supporting projects in every school; this fall it received a record number of applications and funded 77 grants submitted by teachers, parents and student groups. President Mike Cianciolo recognizes the recipients.

**February 1, 2011 minutes.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti, Underwood and Mr. Hauff present, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Rajter, Stromayer, VanDenBerghe and Witt attending, and approximately 25 members of the audience. Philippart thanked Wendy Underwood for leading the Board as president for the past 18 months and for serving on the Board since 2005, presenting a plaque; Underwood noted Philippart has served since the summer of 2008. Resolution 11-019 filled the vacancy for the term ending December 31, 2011: nominations were Kumar Bhatt (Underwood), M'Liz Malven (Hauff) and Bernard Lourim (Miletti); nominations closed 6-0; the Bhatt appointment was defeated 3-3 (Hauff No, Miletti Yes, Philippart No, Underwood Yes, Edmunds Yes, Fleming No) and Malven carried 5-1 (Edmunds No). Resolution 11-020 approved the January 18, 2011 organizational meeting, January 18, 2011 regular meeting and January 21, 2011 retreat minutes, 6-0. Dr. Don VanDenBerghe, principal of Wass Elementary School, presented enrollment projections, which he has provided for the past 29 years. Resolution 11-021 closed Athens High School and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2011/2012 with the exception of not more than 30 ninth grade students living in the Troy High attendance area, plus students with siblings enrolled at Athens in grades 9–11; carried 6-0.

Resolution 11-022 amended the 2010/2011 general appropriations: General Fund $135,897,825; Special Revenue Funds $5,530,101; Debt Service Funds $18,596,717; Capital Projects Fund $7,216,120; Internal Service Fund $120,000. Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, summarized the First Appropriation Act of 2010/2011, said the governor would speak on February 17th with a school aid fund announcement expected in early April, and confirmed Edu-jobs monies are one-time funds fully expended in 2010/2011. Philippart said he was "literally shocked to see that the State has no cash flow." Resolution 11-023 continued Headlee/Adair litigation: Troy is one of 467 school districts in two lawsuits against the State of Michigan alleging underfunding of special education and other mandated services under Article IX, Section 29 of the Michigan Constitution, now pending before the Michigan Supreme Court. Prior authorizations were May 12, 1998 — $5,000; March 2, 1999 — $10,000; June 20, 2000 — $10,000; September 19, 2000 — $10,000; August 20, 2002 — $10,000; February 5, 2008 — $10,000. Secrest, Wardle, Lynch, Hampton, Truex & Morley continues as counsel, with the District's pro rata share not to exceed an additional $5,000. Edmunds noted the District received approximately $5–6 million from the Durant fund; Rajter said the $5,000 should last hopefully 18 months at bills of $300 to $400. Resolution 11-024 awarded carpet replacement to Conventional Carpet for $28,300.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Judy Gail Armstrong-Hall addressed the Board about rocking chairs for classrooms. Kerry Birmingham, Director – Community Relations, presented the 2011/2012 budget communications plan with "Finance 101" sessions on February 8 and February 24 at 7:00 p.m. and quadrant meetings on four consecutive nights in March at the middle schools. A first reading of Board Policy G-1003, Nepotism, was conducted by Mrs. Edmunds, with second reading set for March 1, 2011. Resolution 11-025 authorized closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), carried 6-0; the Board went into closed session at 8:04 p.m., reconvened at 9:36 p.m. and adjourned at 9:37 p.m. Secretary Paula Fleming submitted the minutes. The February 15, 2011 workshop convened at 6:00 p.m. with all seven members and adjourned at 9:35 p.m., covering the Reauthorization Act and new nutritional standards, a Safe-Ed proposal, a facilities study and a budget forecast review.

Fowler, Ph.D. The Board authorized 100 Smart Boards from Smart Ed Services at its March 2, 2010 meeting from a February 2010 bid, installed in summer 2010; volume pricing was to hold one calendar year from award and Bryan negotiated a two week extension. Buildings with sufficient funds — Bemis, Hill, Martell, Schroeder, Troy Union and Wass elementaries plus Athens, Troy High and IA East — want 41 more Smart Board systems for $162,523.78, funded from building internal accounts or PTO donations with none using bond funds. Two requests: 23 Qomo document cameras from City Animation Inc. on the statewide REMC contract for $22,747.00, and 41 Smart Board systems including installation from Smart Ed Services for $139,776.78. The parts list prices an elementary unit at $3,095.38 (SMART SB685 board $1,503.00, Epson 410W projector $570.00, bulb $233.00, wall mount kit $247.06, installation $220.00, among others) for 18 elementary boards at $55,716.84, and a secondary unit at $4,643.78 (adding ProMount kits $220.00, Smart WC6-NA Bluetooth adapter $169.00, DaLite cart $105.40, cart labor $65.00 and the Qomo QD700 camera $989.00) for 23 secondary boards at $106,806.94. **Item 6.A — Personnel.** The Board is asked to accept with appreciation the resignation of Frank Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing & Budget, date of hire December 8, 1999, effective March 14, 2011.

**Item 7.A — District Goals Update.** Presented by Kris Karbon, the District's assessment coordinator and a member of the District NCA Continuous Improvement Team since its inception about five years ago. Forces of change cited are the district continuous improvement cycle, Michigan Department of Education school improvement guidelines and the Common Core State Standards. Current goals: all students create and pursue personal growth plans; all students perceive they are accepted at school regardless of cultural, ethnic, gender, academic or other differences as measured by a validated survey; the District will score in the top 5% on all subtests of MDE assessment programs; all No Child Left Behind subgroups will make Adequate Yearly Progress. All 7th grade students prepare an electronic Educational Development Plan; a Diversity and Inclusion Council was created and the District participates in the Oakland Schools Learning Achievement Coalition–Oakland (LACO). All schools made AYP in all sub-groups in 2009-2010; the top-5% goal "was not met in its entirety." Proposed new goals cover literacy, mathematics, science and social studies college/career readiness.

**Item 7.B — Schools of Choice.** Michigan law requires an annual resolution to participate. Seats are anticipated for 2011-2012 in grades 6–8 at Baker Middle School. Section 105 covers nonresident students from within Oakland County; Section 105c covers students from a district whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries. The resolution cites Section 105 and Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996.

**Item 8.A — Budget Reduction Plan for 2011/2012.** Report by Mark Rajter; no action required. Causes listed: flat or reduced school funding since 2002; increased labor costs; severe revenue cuts in 2009-2010 and 2010-2011; elimination of 20j at $248.18 per pupil ($3 million); and the "Cliff" as ARRA and Education Jobs dollars expired after backfilling the 2009/2010 reduction of $165 per pupil and the 2010/2011 reduction of $154 per pupil. Actions to date: $51.7 million in adjustments since 2002 (Fund Equity $18.6 million, Adjustments $33.1 million); 2009-2010 expenditure cuts of $7.6 million including more than $1 million in mid-year department cuts, 2.5 percent compensation reductions for administrative and non-represented employees, $2 million of deficit covered through Fund Equity, and privatization of custodial, transportation and food services for approximately $3.1 million in annual savings; 2010-2011 expenditure cuts of $6.2 million including 22.4 FTE non-certified and 37.0 FTE certified reductions, higher Pay to Participate fees, privatized grounds and reduced contracted custodial staffing.

Baseline outlook: a projected <$13.6> million operating deficit for 2011-2012, driven by roughly <$500> per pupil in state revenue cuts and increased expenditures — foundation allowance reductions equivalent to $270 per pupil and employer retirement contribution equivalent to $230 per pupil — plus insurance increases equivalent to $217 per pupil and step increases equivalent to $158 per pupil, and reduced county-wide special education revenue under PA 18 of $2.2 million for 2011/2012 and $.3 million for 2012/2013. The long-range plan (including $270 of Governor Snyder's proposed $470 per pupil reduction) shows 2010-2011 with a $0 million deficit, $6.2 million in adjustments and $18.8 million fund equity; 2011-2012 with a $13.6 million deficit, $6.0 million in adjustments, ($7.6 million) of fund equity used and $11.6 million remaining; 2012-2013 with $12.0 million, $8.0 million, ($4.0 million) and $7.6 million; 2013-2014 with $9.1 million, $8.0 million, ($1.1 million) and $6.5 million. Under the Governor's full proposal the deficit becomes <$16.0> million for 2011-2012 at roughly <$700> per pupil with a $470 per pupil foundation reduction, requiring $8.4 million in adjustments in 2011-2012, $10.4 million in 2012-2013 against a $14.4 million deficit, and $10.4 million in 2013-2014 against an $11.5 million deficit.

Proposed 2011/12 reductions and adjustments, tagged (E) for expenditure and (R) for revenue, include: 10% cut to building supply budgets $76,800; maintenance/operations supplies $25,000; custodial supplies $25,000; elimination of 3.35 FTE administrative positions $266,198; restructured athletic offerings and drop-off-only transportation $78,875; athletic supply budget $25,000; restructured Pay to Participate at High School $175 per sport with a $350 max, Middle School $75 per sport with a $150 max and a $600 family maximum, $70,000; transfer of 17% of the Sports Camp account $25,000; PACE restructuring cutting 3.0 FTE $210,189; elementary class-size increase cutting 1.0 FTE $70,063; secondary class-size increase cutting 5.0 FTE $350,316; Schools of Choice IB MYP increase of 25 students $217,069; IB reductions of .5 coordinator and PD expense $60,032; Schedule C stipend cuts of $81,819 (elementary) and $43,000 (secondary); schools of choice K-1 increase of 67 students at $8,682.75 each, $581,744; "Project Search" implemented in consortium with Hazel Park Schools $78,504; non-mandated teacher aides restructured to .5 FTE A.M. only, cutting 6.0 FTE, $280,800; elementary Media Specialists 2.0 FTE $140,126 and middle school Media Specialists 1.20 FTE $84,076; 28 fewer coordinator days $16,316 and 12 fewer counselor days $6,988; two Special Education coordinators at .5 FTE each $70,063; consolidated bus runs $100,000; contracted technology technicians $45,000; two skilled trades positions $122,260; contracted noon aides $39,216; custodial/maintenance schedule restructuring eliminating 4.5 FTE $147,607; 10% sub teacher budget cut $27,000; capture of vending and snack revenue $20,000; administrator and non-rep insurance co-pay $40,000; Community Education fund balance transfer $500,000; HR secretarial cut of at least .5 FTE $27,314; media/technology secretary to .5 FTE $25,409; curriculum secretary to .5 FTE $35,169; and KinderPlus restructured to certified child care providers $150,000. Totals: expenditure reductions $2,748,140; revenue enhancements $1,413,813; total adjustments to revenues and expenditures for 2011/12 $4,161,953; FTE reductions of 17.35 non-certified (administration, TESPA, TESA, non-represented) and 23.20 certified (TEA) for 40.55 total, noted as not indicative of total positions affected. Next steps are informational community meetings at 7:00 p.m. on March 7, 2011 at Baker Middle School, March 8 at Boulan Park Middle School, March 9 at Larson Middle School and March 10 at Smith Middle School.

**Item 11.A — Closed session.** The Board resolves to go into closed session to discuss negotiations as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Philippart, with no additional business afterward other than adjournment.
